senses.gloss:
deśa (IE 8-4; CII 3, 4), a territorial term meaning a small area or a group of villages in some cases but a kingdom, district, tract or country in others.
 (IE 8-4), a country of which there were seventy two^1 in Bhārata or Bhāratavarṣa.
 (CII 1), a part of anything.
 (EI 24), a synonym of āspada.
 (ASLV), a school of music.
 Cf. Kona-deśa (EI 32), also called a maṇḍala, rāṣṭra, sīma, sthala, etc.
 Cf. deśa-bhāṣā (EI 17), ‘vernacular of a province’.
 Cf. teśa-kālam (SITI), locality and time; also teśa-vāl̤i, officer in charge of a village or district.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210207. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/51.

Deś-ādhikṛta (IE 8-3; HD), same as Deśādhipati; governor of a deśa or a province, district or sub-division. See Ep. Ind., Vol. I, p. 5 (Prakrit Desādhikata). See Sarva-deś-ādhikṛta.
 (LL), explained as ‘a local prefect’.
Deś-ādhipati (EI 26, 30), same as Deśādhikṛta; ruler of the territorial or administrative unit called deśa.
Deś-ākṣapaṭalādhikṛta (EI 28), officer of the records and accounts office pertaining to a territorial unit.
Deśakūṭa (AI 7), official designation; cf. Rāṣṭrakūṭa, Grāmakūṭa, Deś-ādhipati.
deśa-maryādā, custom prevalent in a locality; cf. deśa-maryād-ār̤uvaṇa-ānvita (Ind. Ant., Vol. XIX, p. 247, text line 103), ar̤uvaṇa being a tax of six paṇas levied on rent-free lands.
deśanā, Prakrit desanā (EI 21), exposition of the Buddhist doctrine.
deśa-rīta (Chamba), customary taxes of a locality.
Deśa-talāra (LP), probably, a police superintendent. Cf. Talāra.
Deśāyi (ASLV), same as Sanskrit Deśādhipati or Deśādhikṛta.
deśī (EI 11), a guild of local merchants. This is also the name of Prakrit words which are neither Sanskrit (tat-sama) nor derived from Sanskrit (tad-bhava).
Deśilaka, official designation (Ep. Ind., Vol. XIX, p. 71); same as Deśillaka.
Deśillaka (EI 28), official designation as in rāṣtra-grāma-kūṭa-deśillaka-mahattar-ādhikārik-ādīn; same as Desilaka, Deśakūṭa; cf. Purillaka.
deś-ottāra (LP), permission for allowing the cargo to go from one place to another.
deśa-maryād-āruvaṇ-ānvita (Ind. Ant. Vol. XIX, p. 247, text line 103), refers to the right to levy the tax called āruvaṇa (Sanskrit ṣaṭ-paṇa) according to the local custom.
